title: R[x] inside the fraction field of a normal Nagata domain is N-1
statement: Let $R$ be a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] which is a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], let $K$ be its field of fractions, let $x\in K$, and let $S=R[x]\subseteq K$ be the subring of $K$ generated by $R$ and $x$ (an integral domain with field of fractions $K$). Then $S$ is N-1 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]: the integral closure of $S$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

proof.text: Nagata gives Noetherianity of R; the singleton adjoin is finite type, hence S=R[x] is Noetherian. Choose a nonzero denominator a of x. Embed R[x] in the subalgebra R_a of K, identify its localization away from a with R_a using IsLocalization.Away.mk and the localization equivalence, and transfer normality. Every prime localization of this principal open is a normal domain. This is the fully proved private helper adjoin_singleton_normal_away.

Fix a maximal ideal m of S. Supply the proved generator-containing local calculation to the finite-cover lemma, obtaining a finite injective extension A=S_m to a Noetherian domain B with a normal principal open and analytically unramified maximal localizations.
For each maximal q of B, analytic unramifiedness gives N-1. Apply the local N-1 criterion to B and its normal principal open, then descend N-1 along the finite injective extension A to B.
The local N-1 criterion applied to S, its normal principal open and the preceding proof for every maximal localization proves IsN1 S K.
